city.Jamaica.clue.1: couldn't wait to climb a giant staircase of waterfalls that tumble down toward the beach
city.Nicaragua.description: This is the largest country in Central America, known for its chain of smoking volcanoes, a huge freshwater lake with a volcano-island in the middle, and colorful old colonial towns.
city.Nicaragua.landmark: twin volcanic cones of Ometepe Island rising from the waters of Lake Nicaragua at sunset
city.Nicaragua.greeting: Like much of Latin America, people here speak Spanish — say “Hola” (OH-lah).
city.Nicaragua.flag: blue, white, blue with a ring of volcanoes in the middle
city.Nicaragua.clue.0: talked about an island made of two volcanoes sitting in a giant lake
city.Panama.description: This narrow country in Central America links North and South America, and its world-famous canal lets giant ships sail between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans through the thin strip of land.
city.Panama.greeting: People speak Spanish here — say hello with “Hola” (OH-lah).
city.Panama.flag: four squares: a red one, a blue one, and two white ones each holding a star
city.Panama.clue.0: studied a map of a skinny, curving country in Central America
city.Panama.clue.1: kept talking about a huge canal where enormous ships pass between two oceans
city.Panama.clue.2: couldn't wait to visit tiny palm-covered islands where the Guna people live
city.Paraguay.description: This landlocked country in the heart of South America is known for the Guaraní language spoken by nearly everyone, the enormous Itaipú Dam on its rivers, and the wild scrublands of the Gran Chaco.
city.Paraguay.landmark: red-stone ruins of the Jesuit mission of La Santísima Trinidad against a green landscape
city.Paraguay.flag: pinned on a flag badge with red, white, and blue stripes and a little round star emblem in the middle
city.Paraguay.clue.0: asked about buses to a landlocked country in the middle of South America
city.Paraguay.clue.1: practiced speaking Guaraní, an Indigenous language most people there share alongside Spanish
city.Saint Kitts and Nevis.description: This two-island country in the Caribbean is made of green volcanic hills, home to a huge stone fortress high on a hilltop and a sleeping volcano, Mount Liamuiga, wrapped in rainforest.
city.Saint Kitts and Nevis.landmark: stone Brimstone Hill Fortress high above the blue Caribbean
city.Saint Kitts and Nevis.greeting: People here speak English — a warm island “Hello!” works everywhere.
city.Saint Kitts and Nevis.flag: a black diagonal band, two white stars, and green and red triangles
city.Saint Kitts and Nevis.clue.0: wanted to explore a giant stone fortress perched high on a hill above the sea
city.Saint Kitts and Nevis.clue.1: planned to hike up a sleeping volcano with a rainforest crater at its top
city.Saint Lucia.description: This lush island in the eastern Caribbean is famous for the twin Pitons — two pointed volcanic peaks rising straight out of the sea — plus steamy sulphur springs and warm, mineral-rich mud baths.
city.Saint Lucia.landmark: twin green Piton peaks rising steeply from the turquoise sea at Soufrière
city.Saint Lucia.greeting: Many Saint Lucians speak Kwéyòl, a French creole — say hello with “Bonjou” (bon-ZHOO).
city.Saint Lucia.flag: studied a flag in a guidebook: a blue banner with a black-and-yellow triangle shaped like a mountain peak
city.Saint Lucia.clue.0: couldn't wait to see two pointy volcanic peaks poking straight up out of the ocean
